clauses.reason: Section 1 closes the Executive departments, independent establishments and other agencies, including their field services, and excuses employees from duty on Friday, December 26, 1975, with the exceptions in section 2 (which the dossier cut inside this clause). The command is limited by its own terms to that one day, so it was spent at the end of 1975-12-26 (inclusive; the exclusive reading is 1975-12-25).

Section 3 treats Friday, December 26, 1975 as within the scope of Executive Order No. 11582 and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) for pay and leave of employees. It is tied to the same day and was spent at the end of 1975-12-26 (inclusive; exclusive reading 1975-12-25); the pay and leave consequences for that day accrued.

research_rationale:
EO 11891 (signed 1975-12-15) closes Government departments and agencies on Friday, December 26, 1975, with section 2 exceptions for agencies that determine offices should remain open and section 3 pay and leave treatment. The held Federal Register text was read in full; the dossier inventory (section 1 including section 2, and section 3) covers every operative sentence. Each command is limited to December 26, 1975, so each ended by its own terms on 1975-12-26. A search of the held corpus for the number found only the order's own text; no instrument amends or revokes it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No held instrument cites EO 11891 by number; the single-day command could not end earlier than the day it names except by revocation, and none is held.","independent_command_check":"Executive Order 11582 and the statutes cited in section 3 are independent authorities and are not commands of this order.","savings_check":"Pay and leave for the closure day are accrued consequences; no continuing duty.","scope_check":"Sections 1 and 2 (cut as one clause) and section 3 are each confined to December 26, 1975."}

savings.reason: The employees excused on December 26, 1975 and the pay and leave treatment section 3 prescribes for that day accrued on that day; nothing in the order continues after it.
